card.description:

Imagine starting your day on the production floor—checking safety, huddling with supervisors, scanning your ERP dashboard, and walking a focused gemba to spot the next opportunity. By afternoon, you're aligning capacity plans to customer demand, unblocking material flow, and celebrating wins from a cross-functional Kaizen. This is the rhythm of our Director, Manufacturing Operations & Continuous Improvement.

**Your Impact**
---------------

* Build, coach, and mentor a high-performing team of supervisors, leads, and skilled production personnel.
* Champion a culture that prizes safety, quality, accountability, and teamwork.
* Advance engagement through cross-training, development pathways, and clear performance expectations.
* Own production planning, scheduling, and capacity management to meet cost, quality, and delivery goals.
* Ensure on-time manufacturing and shipment while upholding rigorous quality standards.
* Lead Lean, Six Sigma, and CI roadmaps to lift throughput, reduce waste, and standardize best practices.
* Optimize processes to increase productivity and lower cost-to-serve.
* Manage material flow, inventory health, and operational KPIs end-to-end.

* Hands-on expertise with ERP, production planning, scheduling, and inventory management.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, and sound decision-making skills.
* Excellent communicator and people leader.
* Proven ability to drive accountability while fostering a collaborative, positive workplace.

* History of improving productivity, quality, on-time delivery, and employee engagement.

**Who Thrives Here**
--------------------

A visible, floor-engaged leader who blends strategic thinking with hands-on execution. You enjoy solving problems shoulder-to-shoulder with your team and creating an environment where people perform, grow, and stay.

**About Amatrol**
-----------------

We equip learners and employers with hands-on training systems, interactive eLearning, simulators, curriculum, and certification resources that turn complex technology into practical skill. Our U.S.-made solutions serve schools, colleges, training centers, and industry across manufacturing, automation, robotics, electrical systems, oil and gas, packaging, and more—bridging learning and doing for today’s technical careers.

* Six Sigma Experience

* Excellent Communication Skills
* Root Cause Analysis
* Process Development

* Hands On Leadership Style

**Ready to Lead?**

card.title: Director, Co-Manufacturing
card.description:
**Position Summary**

The Director, Co-Manufacturing is responsible for developing, managing, and optimizing Mama's Creations' external manufacturing network to support the company's growth strategy, customer commitments, and operational objectives. This position serves as the enterprise leader for all co-manufacturing relationships, ensuring external partners consistently deliver exceptional service, Grandma Quality, food safety compliance, cost performance, and capacity support.

The Director will build strategic partnerships with contract manufacturers, lead commercialization and capacity expansion initiatives, and ensure co-manufacturing operations align with Mama's values of Commit to Craftsmanship, Nurture Relationships, Honor Heritage, and deliver Grandma Quality.

This role requires a highly collaborative leader who can influence cross-functional partners across Operations, Supply Chain, Procurement, FSQA, R&D, Finance, Sales, and Customer Service while holding external manufacturing partners accountable for operational excellence and business results.

Position can be based in East Rutherford, NJ or Farmingdale, NY

**Co-Manufacturer Strategy & Relationship Management**

* Develop and execute the company's co-manufacturing strategy to support growth, innovation, customer requirements, and capacity needs.
* Identify, evaluate, qualify, negotiate, and onboard new co-manufacturing partners.
* Establish and maintain executive-level relationships with co-manufacturer leadership teams.
* Lead business reviews with co-manufacturing partners, focusing on performance, service, quality, cost, and continuous improvement.
* Ensure clear accountability, governance, and communication structures exist across all manufacturing partners.
* Serve as the primary escalation point for critical business, operational, quality, and supply issues.
* Relationship management and development of multi-site 3PL solution network.

**Operational Performance**

* Own service, inventory, capacity, quality, and cost performance across the co-manufacturing network.
* Establish performance metrics and scorecards to monitor supplier execution and compliance.
* Drive improvements in on-time delivery, schedule adherence, yield, waste reduction, and production efficiency.
* Partner with Supply Planning and Operations teams to align manufacturing capacity with demand forecasts and growth plans.
* Ensure co-manufacturers maintain appropriate labor, equipment, and material resources to support business requirements.

**Commercialization & Product Launches**

* Lead co-manufacturer activities associated with new product commercialization and customer-specific initiatives.
* Partner with Culinary Innovation, R&D, Operations, and FSQA teams to ensure successful product transfers and launches.
* Coordinate production trials, scale-up activities, process validations, and first-production runs.
* Ensure accurate production documentation, specifications, and operational readiness prior to launch.

**Quality, Food Safety & Compliance**

* Partner closely with FSQA to ensure all co-manufacturers consistently meet Mama's food safety, quality, regulatory, and customer requirements.
* Support supplier qualification, audit programs, CAPA activities, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Ensure compliance with FDA, USDA, FSMA, HACCP, GMP, SQF, BRC, and customer-specific standards.
* Lead cross-functional response efforts related to quality events, recalls, customer complaints, or regulatory concerns.

**Financial Management**

* Own co-manufacturing budgets and financial performance.
* Collaborate with Procurement and Finance to negotiate manufacturing agreements and cost structures.
* Identify and execute productivity initiatives that improve margins while maintaining product quality and customer service.
* Evaluate capital and investment opportunities within the co-manufacturing network to support long-term growth.

**Continuous Improvement**

* Develop and implement operational excellence initiatives across manufacturing partners.
* Leverage KPIs, root-cause analysis, and performance reviews to drive sustainable improvement.
* Promote Lean Manufacturing, waste reduction, and process optimization opportunities throughout the network.
* Share best practices among co-manufacturing partners to elevate overall network performance.

**Leadership & Talent Development**

* Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, trust, and continuous improvement.
* Build strong cross-functional partnerships that support enterprise business objectives.
* Serve as a strategic thought partner to Operations leadership regarding network optimization and growth strategies

**Success Metrics**

* The Director, Co-Manufacturing will be measured on:
* Customer service levels
* OTIF (On-Time In-Full) performance
* Product quality performance
* Food safety compliance
* Network capacity utilization
* Manufacturing cost improvement
* Productivity savings
* Commercialization success rate
* Supplier scorecard performance
* Inventory performance
* Customer complaint trends
* EBITDA contribution from network optimization initiatives

**Qualifications**

**Required**

* Bachelor's degree in Food Science, Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Business, or related field.
* 10+ years of progressive manufacturing, supply chain, operations, or co-manufacturing leadership experience.
* Minimum 5 years managing contract manufacturers or external manufacturing networks.
* Experience within food manufacturing, refrigerated foods, CPG, or consumer packaged goods.
* Strong knowledge of FDA, USDA, FSMA, HACCP, GMP, SQF, and food manufacturing operations.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives.
* Strong financial acumen with experience managing budgets, cost optimization, and productivity initiatives.
* Exceptional negotiation, relationship management, and influencing skills.

**Preferred**

* Experience in refrigerated, deli-prepared foods, protein, or fresh food manufacturing.
* Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement certification.
* Experience supporting mergers, acquisitions, or manufacturing network integrations.
* Bilingual English/Spanish.

**Essential Physical Requirements**

* Ability to travel up to 50% of the time to manufacturing partners and company facilities.
* Ability to work within food manufacturing environments, including refrigerated production areas.
* Ability to wear required PPE while conducting plant visits and audits.
* Ability to stand and walk production facilities for extended periods.

card.title: Plant Manager
card.description:
CAMS is looking for a Plant Manager at the Kings Mountain Energy Center in Kings Mountain, NC. The incumbent will have 19 direct and indirect employees. The Plant Manager is responsible for the safe, reliable, compliant, and financially responsible operation and maintenance of the Kings Mountain Energy Center.

Kings Mountain Energy Center is a 475MW natural gas-fired combined-cycle power plant. The facility features an advanced 276MW Mitsubishi M501GAC gas turbine, a Vogt Power heat recovery steam generator (HRSG), a 225MW Toshiba steam turbine generator, and a Thermal Engineering International surface condenser.

The position provides overall leadership for plant operations, maintenance, engineering support, environmental and regulatory compliance, administration, workforce development, budgeting, outage execution, and continuous improvement. The Plant Manager serves as the primary site representative to CAMS leadership, facility ownership and asset management, and is accountable for developing a high-performing organization that maximizes plant availability, reliability, efficiency, and long-term asset value. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong leadership, sound technical and business judgment, and the ability to manage a complex combined-cycle generating facility in a competitive power-market environment.

### **Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* Provide overall leadership and direction for the safe, reliable, environmentally compliant, and cost-effective operation and maintenance of the facility.
* Establish and maintain a strong safety culture in which employees and contractors actively identify hazards, stop unsafe work, and demonstrate personal ownership of safety performance.
* Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental permits, laws, regulations, NERC requirements, OSHA requirements, company policies, and facility procedures.
* Lead and develop the plant management team and workforce, including recruiting, coaching, performance management, succession planning, qualification programs, and workforce development.
* Maintain effective working relationships with facility ownership, Asset Management, CAMS leadership, regulatory agencies, the system operator, utilities, OEMs, contractors, and other key stakeholders.
* Develop and execute annual operating plans, O&M budgets, capital plans, forecasts, and long-term maintenance strategies consistent with owner objectives and contractual requirements.
* Monitor plant financial performance and control expenditures while ensuring that short-term budget objectives do not create unacceptable safety, environmental, reliability, or long-term asset risk.
* Direct plant operations to achieve availability, reliability, heat-rate, start-reliability, capacity, and other performance objectives while meeting dispatch and commercial obligations.
* Provide leadership for maintenance strategies, preventive and predictive maintenance, corrective-maintenance backlog management, equipment reliability, root-cause analysis, and elimination of recurring failures.
* Direct planning and execution of combustion turbine, steam turbine, HRSG, generator, electrical, and balance-of-plant outages and major maintenance activities, including scope, budget, schedule, contractor performance, quality, and risk management.
* Develop and maintain multi-year outage, major-maintenance, and capital improvement plans based on equipment condition, OEM recommendations, operating profile, commercial requirements, and risk.
* Identify significant plant risks and provide CAMS leadership and ownership with timely information, alternatives, consequences, and clear recommendations for decision-making.
* Ensure appropriate critical-spares strategy, inventory controls, long-lead component planning, and equipment-obsolescence management.
* Oversee plant engineering and technical support activities, including equipment modifications, controls and logic changes, performance monitoring, capital projects, and technical problem solving.
* Ensure plant procedures, drawings, technical documentation, training materials, emergency plans, and operating records are accurate and maintained.
* Oversee administration of applicable plant contracts and agreements and ensure operational compliance with owner requirements, O&M obligations, OEM/LTSA requirements, fuel and utility agreements, and other commercial commitments.
* Maintain effective communication with Asset Management and ownership, including prompt escalation of significant safety, environmental, operational, equipment, financial, contractual, or regulatory events.
* Lead emergency response and business-continuity activities and ensure the facility is prepared for severe weather, grid emergencies, fuel interruptions, cyber events, and major equipment failures.
* Promote a culture of accountability, teamwork, continuous improvement, and open communication across Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Compliance, and Administration.
* Identify and implement opportunities to improve plant performance, reduce operating risk, optimize costs, and increase long-term asset value.
* Support CAMS fleet initiatives, peer reviews, lessons learned, workforce-development efforts, and cross-facility technical support as requested.

Other duties as assigned.

### **Qualifications and Skills**

* 10+ years of progressively responsible experience in power generation operations and maintenance, including significant leadership experience in a power plant environment.
* Prior Plant Manager, Operations Manager, Maintenance Manager, or comparable senior power-generation leadership experience strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated knowledge of combined-cycle power plant operations, maintenance, reliability, and major equipment systems. Experience with combustion turbines, steam turbines, HRSGs, generators, electrical systems, and balance-of-plant equipment is preferred.
* Experience with Mitsubishi M501GAC combustion turbines is preferred.
* Demonstrated experience planning and executing major outages, managing contractors and OEMs, controlling outage scope and cost, and resolving emergent technical issues.
* Working knowledge of environmental, health and safety, and electric-generation regulatory requirements applicable to power plant operations.
* Demonstrated experience developing and managing O&M budgets, forecasts, capital projects, and long-term maintenance plans.
* Proven ability to lead, coach, develop, and hold accountable a multidisciplinary workforce.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, decision-making, planning, and organizational skills.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with employees, executives, owners, regulators, contractors, and technical personnel.
* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field preferred. Significant relevant power-generation leadership experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and familiarity with computerized maintenance management systems, plant historians, performance-monitoring systems, and other power-plant business systems.
* Ability to respond to plant emergencies and significant operating events outside normal business hours as required.

Other Desirable Skills

* Demonstrates visible leadership and a strong personal commitment to safety and environmental compliance.
* Balances technical, operational, financial, and commercial considerations when making decisions.
* Communicates significant risks and problems early and avoids surprises for ownership and senior leadership.
* Demonstrates strong customer service skills and the ability to build trusted relationships with facility ownership and Asset Management.
* Effectively prioritizes competing demands in a fast-changing operating environment.
* Develop people and create clear succession paths for key positions.
* Demonstrates a high degree of integrity, accountability, sound judgment, and ownership mentality.
* Ability to represent the facility and CAMS professionally with owners, regulators, industry organizations, and external stakeholders

Applicants must possess a **valid driver's license** and maintain a clean driving record, as this position requires occasional travel for company business. Candidates should be comfortable operating a vehicle as part of their job responsibilities and must meet any applicable company and insurance requirements.

CAMS offers a variety of excellent benefits. Full-time employees are offered the following: medical, dental, vision, LTD, STD, and Life insurance plans. You can even select additional “al la carte” benefits to meet all your needs. You can also enroll in our 401k, flex spending accounts for medical and childcare needs, and participate in our employee referral and tuition reimbursement programs.

Qualified Applicants must be legally authorized for employment in the United States. Qualified Applicants will not require employer sponsored work authorization now or in the future for employment in the United States.

We believe in transparency and providing candidates with important information to make informed decisions. The salary range for this position will be commensurate with experience, qualifications, and location. **POSITION SUMMARY**

The **Director, Contract Manufacturing** reports to the Vice President, Integrated Planning, U.S. Beverage and is based in Cherry Hill, New Jersey.

The Director is responsible for defining the role of contract manufacturing within the Beverage Division’s broader supply network and translating business plans into clear external capacity, capability, geographic, and partnership requirements across the U.S. and Canada. This role leads the development and optimization of the contract manufacturing network to ensure the right capabilities, capacity, cost, quality, service, and resilience to support business growth.

The Director oversees relationships with contract manufacturing partners from initial capability assessment and commercial selection through operational integration, product launch, ongoing governance, and continuous performance improvement.

The Director aligns internal business and functional leaders around external manufacturing decisions and builds productive relationships with strategic partners. The role ensures that external manufacturing resources are positioned to support the division’s growth plans, innovation agenda, service expectations, cost objectives, and business continuity requirements.

**Up to 25% travel required**

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

**External Manufacturing Strategy & Network Optimization**

* Define and execute the contract manufacturing strategy for the Beverage Division across the U.S. and Canada, translating business requirements into external manufacturing capacity, capability, geographic, and partnership needs.
* Optimize the existing contract manufacturing network by assessing manufacturing capabilities, capacity, geographic footprint, technology, cost, service, quality, and supply risk.
* Partner with Integrated Planning, Operations, Finance, Procurement, and other key stakeholders on make-versus-buy decisions and long-term capacity strategies.
* Maintain a strong understanding of the external manufacturing landscape to identify new capabilities, technologies, potential partners, and opportunities to strengthen the overall supply network.

**Strategic Sourcing & Commercial Management**

* Translate business requirements into sourcing strategies for externally manufactured products, balancing economics, available capacity, technical capability, speed, flexibility, and supply risk.
* Lead competitive sourcing and partner-selection activities, including market assessment, RFIs/RFPs/RFQs, commercial evaluation, supplier selection, negotiation, contracting, and implementation.
* Structure and negotiate commercial agreements that clearly define pricing, capacity commitments, service expectations, quality requirements, flexibility provisions, liability, and business continuity obligations.
* Develop fact-based sourcing recommendations considering total cost of ownership, capacity, capability, risk, and overall strategic fit.
* Establish pricing mechanisms and commercial frameworks that promote transparency, competitiveness, and sustainable productivity.
* Provide financial stewardship of external manufacturing spend through disciplined budgeting, forecasting, cost analysis, variance management, and productivity delivery.

**Supplier Relationship & Performance Management**

* Establish and lead a structured Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) approach for strategic contract manufacturing partners.
* Establish and maintain a robust performance management framework and supplier scorecards for the contract manufacturing network.
* Establish a disciplined operating rhythm with strategic partners, supported by agreed performance measures, periodic operating and executive business reviews, documented recovery plans, and clear ownership of actions.
* Build strategic relationships with key external manufacturing partners to improve service, strengthen capacity and flexibility, accelerate innovation, and identify productivity opportunities.
* Lead supplier and network risk assessments and ensure appropriate business continuity, contingency, and risk mitigation plans are developed and maintained.

The Director owns the performance framework for the external manufacturing network, ensuring that targets reflect the division’s priorities for customer service, product quality, delivered cost, productivity, available capacity, launch execution, contractual compliance, and supply continuity. The role is responsible for converting performance information into timely decisions, recovery actions, and clear visibility of results and risks for business leadership.

**Commercialization & Cross-Functional Execution**

* Lead the external manufacturing workstream for new product commercialization, capacity expansions, product transfers, and new contract manufacturer onboarding.
* Partner with R&D, Marketing, Quality, Engineering, Operations, Integrated Planning, and other key functions to ensure new products and external manufacturing capabilities are launched on time, at target cost, and in accordance with quality and regulatory requirements.
* Ensure effective integration of contract manufacturers into the broader planning and supply network, including capacity planning, production planning, inventory management, service, and supply continuity.
* Coordinate resolution of operational and supply issues across internal functions and external manufacturing partners, ensuring clear ownership and escalating material business risks when required.

**Team Leadership & Governance**

* Lead, coach, and develop the Contract Manufacturing team, establishing clear goals, accountability, and individual development plans.
* Establish the governance, processes, tools, decision rights, and performance standards required to effectively manage the external manufacturing network.
* Ensure accurate and actionable contract manufacturing information is maintained, including supplier capabilities, capacity, pricing, commercial terms, products/SKUs, performance, and contractual commitments.
* Provide business leadership with regular visibility into external manufacturing cost, capacity, service, performance, supply risk, and opportunities, enabling timely and informed decision-making.
* Drive cross-functional alignment and accountability for initiatives and decisions affecting the external manufacturing network.

**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE**

**Minimum Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in contract manufacturing, external manufacturing, strategic sourcing, procurement, operations, or supply chain, preferably within the CPG, food, or beverage industry.
* Demonstrated experience managing third-party manufacturing relationships and complex commercial agreements.
* Strong experience in strategic sourcing, supplier negotiations, contracting, and supplier relationship management.
* Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives involving Operations, Planning, Quality, R&D, Finance, Procurement, and Commercial teams.
* Demonstrated ability to evaluate cost, capacity, capability, service, quality, and supply risk and translate analysis into effective business recommendations.
* Strong financial and analytical acumen, including experience with budgeting, forecasting, cost modeling, and productivity initiatives.
* Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and external business partners within a complex matrix organization.
* Strong leadership, communication, negotiation, problem-solving, and change-management skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in the food, beverage, or broader CPG industry.
* Experience managing a multi-site or North American external manufacturing network.
* Experience with new product commercialization, manufacturing transfers, and external partner onboarding.
* APICS/ASCM certification, CPSM, or comparable supply chain/procurement certification.
* MBA or advanced degree.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Directly manages three employees, providing coaching, development, performance management, and clear accountability for results.
* Establishes team priorities, objectives, and performance expectations aligned with the contract manufacturing strategy and broader business goals.
* Builds team capability and expertise while fostering a culture of ownership, collaboration, continuous improvement, and results.
* Provides leadership across a broader cross-functional network, influencing internal stakeholders and external manufacturing partners to achieve service, quality, cost, capacity, innovation, and supply continuity objectives.

* Coordinates plant safety, environmental and training activities in cooperation with the Human Resources Department.
* Comply with company policies and procedures.
